I'll start by profiling the AE and hepatic lab files before building the summary, so I can check the README's counts against the actual data.

<tool_call>{"name": "bash", "arguments": {"command": "mkdir -p /tmp/vdn2847_scripts && cat > /tmp/vdn2847_scripts/profile.py << 'EOF'
import csv, sys, collections
ae_path = '/data/phase3_trial_results/ae_subject_level.csv'
lab_path = '/data/phase3_trial_results/lab_values_hepatic.csv'
with open(ae_path) as f:
    ae = list(csv.DictReader(f))
with open(lab_path) as f:
    lab = list(csv.DictReader(f))
print('AE rows:', len(ae))
print('AE columns:', list(ae[0].keys()))
print('AE ARM counts:', collections.Counter(r['ARM'] for r in ae))
print('AE SEV counts:', collections.Counter(r['AESEV'] for r in ae))
print('AE REL counts:', collections.Counter(r['AEREL'] for r in ae))
print('AE ACN counts:', collections.Counter(r['AEACN'] for r in ae))
print('AE OUT counts:', collections.Counter(r['AEOUT'] for r in ae))
subs = set(r['USUBJID'] for r in ae)
print('Unique AE subjects:', len(subs))
print('Lab rows:', len(lab))
print('Lab ARM counts:', collections.Counter(r['ARM'] for r in lab))
print('Lab VISIT counts:', collections.Counter(r['VISIT'] for r in lab))
print('Lab unique subjects:', len(set(r['USUBJID'] for r in lab)))
print('Unique AEDECOD terms:', len(set(r['AEDECOD'] for r in ae)))
print('--- top AEDECOD by row count ---')
for term, n in collections.Counter(r['AEDECOD'] for r in ae).most_common(40):
    print(n, term)
EOF
python3 -I /tmp/vdn2847_scripts/profile.py"}}</tool_call>
